#1577. Man United next manager: Business as usual for Michael Carrick, but Mauricio Pochettino arrival is 'imminent'

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 09:03

Manchester United are reportedly finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their next head coach, with Michael Carrick expected to be sacked.

A disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, winning just one of their 10 league matches this season.

Man United twice fought back from two goals behind against Aston Villa on Sunday to draw 4-4, but the result is seemingly not enough for Carrick to keep his job.

According to The Athletic, Man United are currently finalising a deal to bring Pochettino to Old Trafford, should Carrick be relived of his duties.

The report claims that the Red Devils spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Pochettino, who is currently in charge of the United States national team.

However, no contact has been made with US Soccer at this stage of proceedings.

It is understood that Man United would need to pay a fee in the region of £7.4m in order to release Pochettino from his contract with the USA.

Further compensation would be required to bring in Pochettino's staff members, which is also expected to be paid, such is Man United's desire to appoint the Argentine.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup, but his time with the national team is seemingly about to end.

The 54-year-old has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, but he has always had a desire to manage the Red Devils.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are set to meet with the club's co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

It is understood that Wilcox and Berrada will recommend to Ratcliffe to remove Carrick from his position at Old Trafford.

Carrick took Man United training on Tuesday and is again at Carrington on Wednesday morning to oversee a session which will largely feature academy players.

Pochettino's first match in charge of Man United is set to be the clash with Liverpool at Anfield after the November international break.

#1576. “Being talked about…”: Everton plotting January move for “interesting” England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1573. Serbia vs Germany - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:13

Germany are under pressure to pick up all three points heading into their penultimate 2026-27 UEFA Nations League group fixture against Serbia on Friday night.

Jurgen Klopp's side are third in Group A2, three points behind second-placed Greece, while Serbia are at the bottom on zero points and cannot qualify for the quarter-finals.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough UEFA Nations League campaign for Serbia, with the national side losing all four of their fixtures in Group A2.

The Eagles opened up with a 2-1 home loss to Greece before going down 2-1 against Netherlands in their second match in the section; a 2-0 loss to Germany followed in their third fixture.

Veljko Paunovic's side were then beaten 2-1 by Netherlands in their last match, and they can no longer finish in the top two in Group A2, although it is still possible to claim third ahead of Germany, with a win required in this match to stand any chance of that occurring.

Serbia have lost each of their last six matches in all competitions, while they have only won once since the end of 2025, so it has been a tough period.

The national side have faced Germany on four previous occasions, boasting a record of one win, one draw and two defeats, with their victory coming in the group stage of the 2010 World Cup.

Germany will know the importance of picking up all three points in this match if they are to stand a chance of securing a top-two spot and advancing to the quarter-finals.

Klopp's side have a record of one win, two draws and one defeat from four games in the section, and they are three points off both second-placed Greece and leaders Netherlands with two matches left.

The National Eleven started their Group A2 campaign with a 1-1 draw against Netherlands before suffering a shock 1-0 home loss to Greece at the end of September.

Germany managed to post an important 2-0 win over Serbia at the start of October, but they were then held to a goalless draw by Greece, so DFB-Team are playing catch-up ahead of their final two fixtures against Serbia and Netherlands.

Anything less than four points from their final two matches would make qualification highly unlikely, but successive wins would take them onto 11 points and could potentially be enough to advance to the final eight of the Nations League.

Serbia will be without the services of two players through suspension, with Sasa Lukic and Nemanja Maksimovic ruled out of the contest with Germany.

Aleksandar Mitrovic is in line to win his 107th cap for his country, and the 32-year-old could be joined in the final third of the field by Mihajlo Cvetkovic, who has one goal in five matches for Serbia.

There is also set to be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Sergej Milinkovic-Savic.

Germany, meanwhile, have three players one booking away from a suspension, with Philipp Treu, Malick Thiaw and Yann Bisseck all in danger of missing the team's final fixture in the group stage of the 2026-27 Nations League.

Kai Havertz has scored 25 times for Germany and is once again expected to feature through the middle, while Florian Wirtz could also be in line for a starting role on Friday.

Said El Mala and Lennart Karl could be involved from the first whistle, while Marc-Andre ter Stegen has been confirmed as Germany's number one goalkeeper.

V Milinkovic-Savic; Nedeljkovic, Gudelj, Babic, Erakovic, Sukacev; Samardzic, S Milinkovic-Savic, Zivkovic; Cvetkovic, Mitrovic

Ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Nmecha, Kimmich; El Mala, Wirtz, Karl; Havertz

Germany have been far from convincing in this Nations League tournament, but Serbia have also struggled, and we are backing Klopp's side to secure a valuable three points on Friday.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1569. Luxembourg vs Estonia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 10:10

Estonia square off against Luxembourg on Friday evening knowing that victory could guarantee them a top-two spot in UEFA Nations League Group C4.

However, despite sitting bottom of the group, Luxembourg can move level on points with their second-placed opponents with a win in Luxembourg City.

Although Iceland were the favourites for this group before it began, it was an evenly-match draw that gave chances to all four nations.

That is how it has panned out, with bottom-placed Luxembourg trailing leaders Iceland by five points with two matches remaining.

Luxembourg began their campaign with a 2-1 victory in Bulgaria, but losing 3-0 at home to Iceland in their following fixture seemingly dented their belief.

Further defeats to Estonia and Bulgaria, without scoring a goal, have extended their losing streak to three games, yet they remain in a position where they could earn a spot in the promotion playoffs.

Jeff Strasser's side remain 21 places above Estonia in the FIFA World Rankings in 101st position, a consequence of having won four of five matches prior to their recent run without success.

However, Estonia are currently on a six-game unbeaten streak, a period where they have conceded just the one goal.

While their solitary success in this group is a 1-0 triumph over Luxembourg in the reverse fixture, Jurgen Henn's team have twice held Iceland to low-scoring draws and also shared the spoils with Bulgaria.

If Estonia beat Luxembourg and Iceland win in Bulgaria on Friday, they will be guaranteed a place in the promotion playoffs with one match to spare.

Each of their last three wins on the international stage have been by 1-0 scorelines.

With Dick Carlson serving a one-match ban for accumulating two yellow cards, Florian Bohnert could move into the middle of the Luxembourg backline.

That would allow captain Laurent Jans to return at right-back after he missed the last two matches due to injury.

Sebastien Thill and Aiman Dardari are alternatives in midfield and the final third if Strasser wants to make further alterations.

There will be at least two changes to the Estonia XI with Marten Kuusk and Robi Saarma not featuring in Henn's squad.

Captain Karol Mets could slot into the back three, while Karel Mustmaa may be introduced into the attack.

Mattias Kait - the only player in the Estonia squad with more than three international goals - is an option to return in central midfield.

Moris; Jans, Bohnert, Selimovic, Veiga; Cruz; Natami, V Thill, Dos Santos, Kadamani; Videira

Igonen; Mets, Paskotsi, Tougjas; Peetson, Palumets, Kristal, Poom, Saliste; Mustmaa, Mannilaan

With Estonia having shown their defensive quality at this level, it will be difficult for Luxembourg to get on the scoresheet. After Estonia beat Luxembourg by the solitary goal in their first meeting in October, we feel that a repeat scoreline could occur here.

#1568. Embattled FIFA chief Gianni Infantino 'used Trump adviser to get work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper'

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 15:01 EST, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 9 November 2026

FIFA President Gianni Infantino allegedly influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

The Nicaraguan-born Fernandez was reportedly employed by the soccer governing body to work as a housekeeper for the FIFA boss and his family in August 2024. Despite being on FIFA's payroll, she performed no services for the organization.

However, she reportedly continued illegally working in her role and living in the Infantino household for months after the Trump administration terminated the immigration agreement that granted her permission to stay in the United States.

Fernandez is then said to have secured a new work authorization under Kristi Noem's Department of Homeland Security following an intervention by a Trump adviser, documents show.

Infantino allegedly tapped Carlos Cordeiro, the former US Soccer chief who served as a senior World Cup adviser to Donald Trump, to orchestrate the new work permit.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino (right) reportedly enlisted the help of a Trump adviser to secure a work permit for his family's Nicaraguan housekeeper

Infantino allegedly tapped Carlos Cordeiro (pictured) to orchestrate a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez

In January, Infantino reportedly asked Cordeiro, who in May 2025 was appointed to the White House's World Cup task force alongside Noem, to use his connections at the state department to smooth the path to getting Fernandez's new work visa approved, according to the documents.

Cordeiro also allegedly first helped to secure Fernandez's right to work in the US under Infantino's orders in 2024.

Fernandez was reportedly already living and working at Infantino's residence in Miami, Florida, in early 2024.

However, until May 2024, she had not yet filed or received an approved work permit and was therefore working at the residence illegally, per the documents.

During a January 2024 meeting at Infantino's home, Cordeiro, at the FIFA boss's request, is said to have instructed a subordinate to submit their own Miami rental address on Fernandez's immigration filing rather than that of the Infantino family home.

While Fernandez's work visa was initially approved, it came to an abrupt end last year when the Department of Homeland Security terminated the Humanitarian Parole Program for Cuba, Haiti, Venezuela and her native Nicaragua.

On May 30, 2025, the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to scrap the four-country scheme, which had permitted Fernandez and other Nicaraguans to secure permission to work in the US.

Fernandez's contract with FIFA was terminated in October 2025, but she was paid a three-month salary as a bonus and remained illegally working as Infantino's housekeeper for the remainder of the year, according to the documents.

Cordeiro (left) was appointed to Trump's White House's World Cup task force in 2025

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem worked in connection with the task force

In January 2026, Infantino allegedly asked Cordeiro, who was now working on the World Cup task force which operated directly out of Homeland Security, to leverage his new government contacts to secure Fernandez a new permit. That same month, Fernandez was granted a new work visa.

There is no suggestion that Fernandez personally is accused of any wrongdoing.

FIFA strongly denied the allegations that it had 'employed an individual in the US without the necessary authorisation.'

'FIFA verifies the employment status of each employee and ensures compliance with U.S. immigration and employment requirements,' a FIFA spokesperson told The Daily Mail.

'Matters related to the FIFA President's personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the FIFA President personally.

The organization added: 'As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.'

Cordeiro did not immediately respond to The Daily Mail's requests for comment. However, he declined to address his alleged role to The New York Post, claiming he was 'not aware of the story.'

In a statement to the Daily Mail, a spokesperson for the DHS said: 'On December 16, 2023, Yajarlin del Socor Fernandez, an alien from Nicaragua, was permitted entry into the United States through the now-defunct Biden-era CHNV parole program.

'Del Socor Fernandez re-applied for lawful status in December 2025 and was approved to remain in the United States until January 2027.'

Infantino, who is standing for reelection in 2027, has faced months of scrutiny

The bombshell report comes after months of scrutiny for Infantino, who faces reelection in 2027.

Infantino faced mutiny earlier this year over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

It sparked uncertainty around Infantino's future after three confederations rejected his plan, which was then abandoned.

Among them was UEFA, which said it has lost confidence in Infantino and threatened to boycott future World Cups.

Cordeiro also recently quit FIFA over Infantino's commercial deals with Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital.

Infantino faced further scrutiny last month when it was alleged that Infantino personally intervened to suspend USA Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card following a call with President Trump.

In a saga that sparked condemnation from across the world, the striker was originally barred from the USA's last-16 match against Belgium, only for his ban to be sensationally suspended by the FIFA disciplinary committee following a protest by the White House. The New York Post claimed in October that Infantino told Trump in a call on July 1 that 'he would take care of it. One call and it was done.'

FIFA did not comment on the claims at the time but pointed to a July statement from Infantino, when he insisted the decision was made by 'independent' bodies acting 'autonomously.'

Despite mounting pressure over recent months, Infantino intends to stand for a fourth consecutive term next March at the FIFA Congress.

#1566. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1563. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 10:40, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:40

England Under-21s and Portugal Under-21s square off in an international friendly at Ashton Gate on Friday night.

These nations have booked their place at the European Under-21 Championship next summer.

While England Under-21s have won the last two European Championships, they are not showing the kind of form which suggests that they can win a third crown in a row.

Even prior to losing 3-1 in Republic of Ireland in their most recent fixture, Lee Carsley had witnessed his team held to a 1-1 draw in Andorra and only record a 4-2 triumph over Kazakhstan on home territory.

Just one clean sheet has been kept in five games, that coming in a goalless draw at home to Slovakia.

Although England did enough to win their qualification group with a game to spare, their defensive record indicates that they will be outsiders when it comes to the next major tournament.

Only one defender in this squad - Chelsea's Josh Acheampong - is earning regular Premier League football, emphasising the size of the task that they have to overcome a nation such as Portugal.

Luis Freire's have hardly been perfect themselves, with a 2-1 defeat to Bulgaria having been posted in September.

However, Portugal have incredibly won their other 10 matches across an 11-game period with a clean sheet.

Either side of the Bulgaria setback, 10 goals have been netted in fixtures versus Northern Ireland, Gibraltar and Czech Republic.

As much as Carsley's team need to test themselves against opposition of the level of Portugal, Freire will want to see how his players handle England's attacking flair.

These teams last squared off as recently as March 2025, with England recording a 4-2 victory at The Hawthorns.

Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni, Arsenal winger Max Dowman and Norwich City's Jovon Makama are all hoping to earn their first caps.

Liverpool continue to assess potential additions to their attacking options as the club looks towards future transfer windows. One name attracting attention is Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, although the Reds could face serious competition from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

#1559. Moldova vs Kazakhstan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 10:54, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:56

Moldova and Kazakhstan will continue their respective 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaigns with a contest in Group C3 on Friday night.

Neither team can finish at the top of the section and secure automatic promotion to League B, but the pair are both in the running to qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Moldova have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in Group C3, with four points leaving them in third position in the table.

The Tricolours are level on points with second-placed Faroe Islands and will have their eyes on second spot, which would see them qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Lilian Popescu's side started their Group C3 campaign with a 2-0 loss to Slovakia, before drawing 1-1 with Faroe Islands ahead of a 2-1 victory over Kazakhstan.

Moldova will enter this match off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Slovakia, and they are now preparing for their final two games in the section against Kazakhstan and Faroe Islands.

The Tricolours have only actually won one match since November 2024, which proved to be their 2-1 success over Kazakhstan in the reverse game between the two sides.

As for Kazakhstan, a record of two draws and two defeats has left them at the bottom of Group C3 on two points, two points behind second-placed Faroe Islands.

The Hawks started their 2026-27 Nations League campaign with a 1-1 draw against Faroe Islands before suffering back-to-back losses to Slovakia and Moldova.

John van 't Schip's side will enter this match off the back of a 2-2 draw with Faroe Islands, and they are currently on a run of six games without a victory.

Kazakhstan have a record of three wins, two draws and three defeats against Moldova in all competitions, with three of their last six games being won by the former.

The Hawks will finish their Group C3 campaign at home to Slovakia on November 16.

Moldova have no players suspended for this match, but Iurie Iovu, Vadim Rata and Oleg Reabciuk are one booking away from missing the team's next game.

Petru Popescu has scored twice in eight appearances for his country and is once again expected to feature in the final third of the field on Friday.

There should also be a start in midfield for Nichita Motpan.

As for Kazakhstan, Sergey Malyy is suspended for Friday's match following his red card in the team's last fixture in the competition.

Ramazan Karimov and Galymzhan Kenzhebek are set to feature in the final third of the field on Friday, while Georgi Zhukov will be a notable starter in a deeper area for the visitors.

#1558. GdS: ‘Ahead of the curve’ – Amorim’s positive start compared to predecessors

Ruben Amorim might not have unanimously won everyone over yet, but AC Milan are off to their best Serie A start in four years.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write this morning that Milan under Amorim have started better than under Massimiliano Allegri in 2025-26, Paulo Fonseca in 2024-25 and even Stefano Pioli’s final season in 2023-24.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The best start belongs to the coach who delivered the Scudetto though, with 31 points in the first eleven rounds of the 2021-22 season, which ended with the most recent Italian league title added to the trophy cabinet.

Amorim has also hit the ground running, with an average that, in previous seasons, would have placed him even higher. A year ago, with 24 points at this same stage of the tournament, Milan would have been the league leaders.

The numbers don’t lie: 24 out of a possible 33 points – garnered through seven wins, three draws, and only one Serie A defeat – amount to 2.18 points per match. By comparison, Allegri had reached 22 points, Fonseca 17 and Pioli also had 22 in his final year.

The coach behind the 2021-22 Scudetto also started with great momentum in the previous season (26 points in 2022-23) and in the 2020-21 campaign (27 points).

These figures were double the 13 points from the 2019–20 season, a campaign that began with Marco Giampaolo at the helm, only for him to be replaced mid-season by Pioli. While still seeking to find that same rhythm in Europe, Milan have been surging in the league.

They got off to a blistering start with wins away at Torino and in their San Siro debut against Venezia, followed by a draw at Juventus – a match in which they were pegged back just minutes from the end -and another stalemate away to Lazio.

After falling two goals behind, Milan fought back against the team currently leading the league. Given Lazio’s subsequent form, that result takes on added significance. Next came a victory over Lecce, followed by a lacklustre draw in Reggio Emilia against Sassuolo.

From that point on, the turning point arrived: four wins in the next five matches, including away victories against Udinese and Genoa away from home, as well as the derby. The only stumble during this stretch was against Bologna.

Sensing that the squad was under significant stress, Amorim has granted a week off, with training set to resume next Monday. For those without other commitments such as international duty, this provides a chance to truly switch off.

Many players have headed away, while those who remained are either following strict injury recovery programs or simply taking a break. This pause is longer than usual: the typical break in professional leagues is generally shorter.

This isn’t the only unusual aspect: the return to training ahead of the match against Frosinone the following week will also take place only after the players returning from international duty have been given ample time to rest.

There are precedents for this, though. For instance, the team was given a Tuesday off just two days before their European away match against Bournemouth. They returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they departed for England. The result was a 3-0 loss and a dark night.

There is certainly enough evidence now to speak of new methods introduced by Amorim and his staff. On the pitch, Rúben has brought in new ideas: training sessions are never overly gruelling, and the data from GPS trackers and distance-monitoring tools is never pushed to ‘excessive’ levels.

“We train by playing,” the Portuguese coach has often explained, implying that matches themselves offer the best opportunities to test tactical schemes and movements. This is especially the case when playing every three days, with such little time between games.

While this approach may have initially raised some eyebrows among the players and was even speculated to be a cause for the cluster of injuries the Rossoneri experienced, such concerns were dispelled once the coach provided further clarification.

In the meantime, no one is taking a break fully. Even while away, every player has been assigned specific training programs to follow, ensuring they return in peak condition to keep the good league form going.

#1557. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1556. Celtic 1 Kilmarnock 0: Liam Scales scores only goal as Premiership leaders make hard work of it

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026

For Martin O’Neill, the second international break of the season should be somewhat less fretful than the first.

Seven weeks ago, with a home defeat to Ferencvaros coming in between two no-shows against Rangers, the veteran wondered aloud if it might be time to ‘wrap it up’.

O’Neill later admitted that he regretted his choice of words. He won’t, though, lament the decision to go again as he rests up in the coming days.

While the intervening weeks have often been a bumpy ride, the past four days have been a lot more like it.

Thursday’s dramatic win over Besiktas has breathed new life into Celtic’s Europa League campaign.

While by no means spectacular, this narrow victory over Kilmarnock re-established their four-point lead at the top of the Premiership and will have further dampened the sense of hysteria which was threatening to engulf the entire club.

Celtic defender Liam Scales loops the ball over Kilmarnock's goalkeeper and into the net

Scales celebrates with Camilo Duran after netting the only goal of the game at Celtic Park

Celtic striker Kasper Hogh finds the net with a crisp right-foot shot, only to have it disallowed

Celtic certainly made hard work of this. Truth be told, they should have gone into the break on the back of a far more convincing victory.

While they were right to feel wronged that Kasper Hogh saw his goalless run stretch to 16 matches after having one harshly disallowed, O’Neill’s men did not help themselves either.

Coming after Liam Scales had given them a half-time advantage, Benjamin Nygren’s missed penalty allowed Kilmarnock to keep believing right to the end.

Nonetheless, it was hard to begrudge Celtic their victory over the piece. A few weeks back, this might have been a contest in which they’d have come a cropper. They look more assured defensively than earlier in the season.

You don’t need to stay up all night researching exactly why Kilmarnock are in such peril at this stage of the season.

Neil McCann’s side began the campaign losing goals and they’ve really never stopped. They cough up more chances than any side in the top division. When it comes to shooting themselves in the foot, they’re in a league of their own.

In 13 games to date, they’ve shipped 29 goals and have kept just two clean sheets in the process. St Mirren, the side with the second worst record in the Premiership, have lost 22.

As worrying as those statistics and the Premiership table undoubtedly are, though, this felt like a step in the right direction.

In being more resolute, McCann’s men stayed in the contest right until the final whistle. They fashioned a number of decent chances throughout. There was plenty of encouragement here, even though they went down again.

For the home supporters, the much-needed positivity which had emanated from Thursday’s European win was boosted by the return to the starting line-up of Jota for the first time since April 2025.

Notably, only three out of nine of Celtic’s summer signings made the squad, with Sam Johnstone the only one involved who arrived on deadline day.

O’Neill was indebted to the on-loan Wolves man inside the first minute. Ieuan Owen skipped away from Callum McGregor then Colby Donovan down the left and put in a dangerous cross. Twice Tom Lowery hit the target. Twice the Celtic keeper stood up tall.

Lowery immediately had his name taken by John Beaton for a clumsy foul on Nygren.

Despite their precarious position, to their credit, Kilmarnock didn’t come to Parkhead just to defend. Tyreece John-Jules, their main striker, had an abundance of support in the form of Owen, Greg Kiltie and Joe Hugill.

Between them, they fashioned enough half chances. They just didn’t have ice in the veins at the right moments.

Hogh was right to feel aggrieved at the decision which cost him that elusive goal. Truthfully, there was very little in Mika Baur’s challenge on Kiltie which was retrospectively penalised.

Duran gathered and fed Nygren. The Swede swivelled and rolled the ball into Hogh’s path. A crisp right-foot finish was not that of a player lacking in confidence.

The Dane’s lengthy celebrations included a look up to the heavens. By the time Beaton made his way to the monitor and chalked the goal off, Hogh could have been forgiven for feeling that someone up there had it in for him.

To Hogh’s credit, he didn’t let it affect him. Moments later, after being played in by Duran, he was only denied his revenge by the outstretched leg of Nico Mantl.

Hogh then played Duran in with a clever back-heel. The Colombian lashed his effort just wide.

Celtic’s pressure was mounting and they edged in front on 26 minutes with Duran, yet again excellent throughout, the architect.

His clipped cross from the right caught the Kilmarnock defence flat-footed. Scales extended his left foot and watched the ball rise to the point where it appeared to be going over.

With Mantl hoping that it would clear his bar, it looped into the net. There was no disputing this one.

Required to take more risks, Killie had to be careful when they turned the ball over. Hugill and Cathal McCarthy were both booked for crude fouls on Duran and Jota, respectively.

While Celtic began to control the affair, the visitors were not without their moments. Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s stinging strike from 25 yards forced Johnstone into another solid stop.

While Jota looked good in moments, it’s clearly going to take some time before he’s fully up to speed. The same might apply to Hyun-jun Yang, the man who replaced him at the interval, after being sidelined for six weeks with a hamstring injury.

Donovan came close to wrapping up the three points with an enterprising run and shot with his left foot which flew just wide.

Duran’s close control and speed across the ground bought him a yard for a shot. Having seen it late, Mantl dealt with it well.

Hogh actually performed well here. He was tidy with the ball and frequently brought team-mates into play. He just didn’t hit the target often enough. That again cost him when he spun neatly in the box and tried his luck midway through the second period.

You couldn’t fault him when he seized on Kieran Tierney’s cross, though. The saving block from Killie substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara was tremendous.

With the home supporters longing for a clinching second goal, Duran dumped a shot into the side netting before the industrious Baur was flagged offside after firing home.

The wait would go on. Initially adjudged to have struck Aaron Tshibola’s arm just outside the box, Yang’s strike would earn Celtic a spot-kick with 14 minutes remaining after a VAR review.

Nygren just never looked confident as he spotted the ball. Mantl dived to his right and made a comfortable save. Those hoping for a sharp exit sat back in their seats.

The sight of Baur hobbling badly after being caught by Tshibola didn’t make the viewing in the final moments any easier. All that truly counted for the home fans, though, was that Celtic got over the line.
